newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AGA CEO sees significant cost savings.
newsitem.headline: AGA CEO sees significant cost savings.

text.p: Swedish medical and industrial gas maker AGA AB's new, more efficient organisation will mean significant cost savings, said the company's chief executive officer (CEO) Lennart Selander.
"I cannot say how large cost savings it (the new organisation) concerns, but we are talking about significant numbers," Selander told Reuters.

Earlier on Thursday, the company said it was reorganising the company with operations to be divided into three business areas -- manufacturing industry, process industry and health care -- in a bid to boost profitability.
In 1997, the effect of the reorganisation on earnings might be positive or negative, Selander said.
"(The reorganistion involves) partly cost cuttings and partly certain restructuring costs, but I cannot say whether the effect will be positive or negative...It is up to us," he said.

On March 3, when the company is due to release 1996 earnings, Selander said he expected to be able to give a forecast for the full-year 1997 and more exact figures regarding the effects of the reorganisation.
